WITH RITA'S CREDIT BESIDE THE PLATES. PLACE THE PA
AT THE WALL FACING THE HOUSE, AND THE SCREEN AT
pages.raw_text: Put the carrier and serving table under the hatch, with Rita’s credit beside the plates. Place the PA at the wall facing the house, and the screen at

pages.text:
THE MARKED DISPLAY ALCOVE. KEEP THE GATE LANE
CLEAR, THEN TELL FRANKIE YOU'RE READY.
pages.raw_text: the marked display alcove. Keep the gate lane clear, then tell Frankie you’re ready.

pages.text:
RITA AND I ARE GOING BACK TO THE CONSERVATORY TO
FINISH SOMETHING. WE'LL BE CLOSE BY.
pages.raw_text: Rita and I are going back to the conservatory to finish something. We’ll be close by.

pages.text:
WE'LL BRING MY DISPLAY WHEN IT'S TIME. KEEP ITS
PLACE HIDDEN FOR ME.
pages.raw_text: We’ll bring my display when it’s time. Keep its place hidden for me.

pages.text: I'LL PUT OUT THE WELCOME SNACKS IN THE KITCHEN.
pages.raw_text: I’ll put out the welcome snacks in the kitchen.

pages.text: I'LL CHECK OUR CUES AT THE LIVING-ROOM BOARD.
pages.raw_text: I’ll check our cues at the living-room board.

speech.raw_text: Everything’s ready. The buffet should be the first thing the guests see.
I should be the first thing. I invited them.
And their first step lands where? The buffet, sound and display can’t all have the doorway. Doorways are for walking.
You stand in them when you’re right.
So everybody hears. Now let’s leave this one clear.
Right. The plans show where everything fits.
Chevrons mark the clear gate-to-house lane. Guests must be able to get past the first person who wants to explain something.
The tray mark is below the kitchen hatch: food through the hatch, buffet underneath. My cooking can make an entrance without me blocking the door.
The sound mark is by the wall. The speaker faces inward toward our courtyard and the house. The neighbor is allowed to have a different evening.
A panel-shaped footprint in the alcove. Vivian’s mark shows where the screen conceals it from arriving guests.
A serving table I can push or pull under the hatch, into the tray footprint. Easier to move than a guest who has started telling you
something.
The kitchen hatch and buffet position share a tray symbol. Keep the hatch in clear view. I want people admiring the food before they start asking
what’s in it.
Three placements, one clear route: buffet at the hatch, sound facing inward, screen at the display alcove. Keep the chevrons empty.
The carrier is at the buffet below the hatch. Rita’s plates can be laid out here.
Plates laid out. The padding’s free to go back to the kitchen.
The PA is at the marked wall, facing into the courtyard. An announcement of supper for people who are actually getting some.
The screen conceals the display alcove. The gate lane and kitchen view stay clear.
The serving table is under the hatch, inside the tray footprint.
The serving table is under the hatch, inside the tray footprint.
Rita’s name, right beside her work. The credit gets to stay on show after I cover everything else in gravy.
That blocks the gate-to-house lane. Move it off the chevrons so people can walk through. We can’t ask them to arrive sideways.
That hides the kitchen hatch. Move the screen to the marked display alcove; only Rita’s display needs hiding. If Bunny can’t see dinner, I’ll
never hear the end of it.
The grille points at the neighbor. Turn it inward, toward our courtyard and the house. At the moment our best seat is next door.
Arrivals can see the display before Rita has chosen her moment. Use Vivian’s marked side of the alcove. Rita hasn’t practised looking modest for
nothing.
We can get through. We can hear. We can serve.
It works.
And everybody I invited is coming to the same evening.
With room to get their supper without turning sideways.
Rita’s panel stays hidden until after the meal, when she presents it.
Agreed.
Buffet and Rita’s credit at the hatch. Sound facing inward. Screen in the alcove. Gate lane clear.
And eight tasting portions ready in the kitchen.
Good. Shall we begin?
Rita and I are going back to the conservatory to finish something. We’ll be close by.
We’ll bring my display when it’s time. Keep its place hidden for me.
I’ll put out the welcome snacks in the kitchen.
I’ll check our cues at the living-room board.
